title: How to Start a Skilled Nursing Facility in California: Complete Licensing Guide

html:
Starting a skilled nursing facility in California requires significant investment and regulatory navigation. With 1,230 licensed facilities and 87% occupancy, opportunities exist in underserved areas.

Understanding California SNF Regulations

CDPH Licensing and Certification Division regulates SNFs. Facilities must obtain state licensure and Medicare/Medi-Cal certification.

Licensing and Certification

Complete CDPH licensure through comprehensive application, construction approval, and survey process. Obtain Medicare and Medi-Cal certification. Process takes 18-36 months.

Business Planning

Development costs range from $150,000-$300,000 per bed. Medi-Cal reimburses approximately $246/day. Margins of 2-7% require operational efficiency.

Facility Requirements

Meet Life Safety Code, accessibility standards, and CDPH space requirements. Design for quality care and regulatory compliance.

Staffing

Employ DON, licensed nurses, CNAs, and support staff. Meet California staffing ratio requirements. Address workforce challenges.

Quality and Compliance

Maintain Five-Star ratings through health inspections, staffing, and quality measures. Implement robust QAPI programs.
